Simulate one pyramidal tract (one hemisphere) as a fiber::bundle_set

Source: R/pyramid.R
simulate_pyramidal_tract.Rd

Generates the pyramidal tract of a single hemisphere as a fiber::bundle_set: five per-parcel bundles (leg, trunk, arm, hand, face) laid out by the somatotopic table pyt_defaults(). Each parcel is a centreline swept along a common macro-axis with a smooth (C1) moving frame, then perturbed into a bundle of axons with create_axons().

Usage

simulate_pyramidal_tract(
  parcels = NULL,
  macros = NULL,
  rot_st = NULL,
  cross = NULL,
  perturbation = NULL,
  hemisphere = "left",
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

parcels

Optional character vector of parcel names to include (defaults to all five from pyt_defaults()).

macros

Optional list with tract_length, midline_offset, bow, n_points (defaults from pyt_defaults()).

rot_st

Optional numeric control points for the twist map psi (length equal to nrow(pyt_defaults()$q_st)).

cross

Optional list with cross_percent, cross_span, cross_detour, center_gap.

perturbation

Optional list with variance, autocorrelation, n_basis, n_axons (reused by create_axons()).

hemisphere

Either "left" or "right"; the medial wall faces the midline (+X toward the neighbour hemisphere).

seed

Optional integer seed for full reproducibility.

Value

A fiber::bundle_set of one bundle per parcel. Each stream's streamline_data carries parcel and branch (crossed/uncrossed).

Details

The face parcel terminates at the pons (corticobulbar); the limb/trunk parcels continue through the decussation into the cord. Each parcel contains a crossed and an uncrossed branch: the crossed branch's q is multiplied by a smooth sign-flip phi(s) (default 85% of fibers cross), nudged laterally by center_gap (mm, so the two copies interlace at the decussation) and pushed posteriorly by cross_detour (mm, the interdigitating X), without any streamline splitting (D1) or fusion (C3).

Examples

pyt <- simulate_pyramidal_tract(hemisphere = "left", seed = 1)
fiber::is_bundle_set(pyt)      # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE
